'''Nalögo''' ({{IPA|nlz|nalɵᵑgo}}) is an [[Oceanic language]] spoken on the island of [[Nendö]] in the [[Solomon Islands]]. It used to be lumped together with [[Natügu language|Natügu]] under a single language called the "Santa Cruz language", but the two varieties were recognized to be two distinct languages in 2012.<ref name="BZ">{{cite journal|last1=Boerger|first1=Brenda H.|last2=Zimmerman|first2=Gabrielle|title=Recognizing Nalögo and Natügu as separate languages: Code-splitting in ISO 639-3|journal=Journal of the Linguistic Society of Papua New Guinea|volume=30|issue=1|pages=95-132|date=January 2012|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/291345040_Recognizing_Nalogo_and_Natugu_as_separate_languages_Code-splitting_in_ISO_639-3}}</ref>

Together, Nalögo, [[Natügu]] and [[Nanggu]] are the three indigenous languages of Nendö island.

Nalögo has been described by linguist Valentina Alfarano.<ref name="grammar">{{Harvcoltxt|Alfarano|2021}}.</ref>

==The language==
===Name===
The name ''Nalögo'' (new orth. ''Nalrgo'') comes from ''nalö-go''  {{IPA|nlz|nalɵᵑgo|}}, literally "our language"<ref name="BZ" /> – from ''nalö'' "language, word" + ''-go'' "[[Grammatical number#Minimal, unit augmented, and augmented|1st + 2nd person augmented]] enclitic").

===Genetic affiliation===
Like its neighbours Natügu and Nanggu, Nalögo was once thought to be dialects of a language labelled “Santa Cruz”; and the latter was long thought to be a [[East Papuan languages|Papuan language]]. In the 2000s however, it became clear that was shown to be a member of the [[Austronesian languages|Austronesian]] language family, like the rest of the [[Reefs – Santa Cruz languages]].<ref>{{cite journal 
| last1= Næss
| first1= Åshild
| author2= Brenda H. Boerger
| title= Reefs – Santa Cruz as Oceanic: Evidence from the verb complex
| journal= Oceanic Linguistics
| year= 2008
| volume= 47
| pages= 185–212 
| doi= 10.1353/ol.0.0000 
| hdl= 1959.13/1052427
| hdl-access= free
}}</ref>

===Dialects===
Nalögo and Natügu are recognised as opposite ends of a [[dialect continuum]].<ref name="BZ" /> The Nalögo section of the dialect chain includes two named dialects, Nea and Nooli.

Nalögo has the same consonants as those of neighbouring [[Natügu language|Natügu]] – with the addition of {{IPA|nlz|ⁿd​͡ʒ}}.

Prenasalized stops can optionally be realized as plain voiced consonants.<ref name="grammar" />{{rp|43}}
